title: Financing Account Standing and the Late-Rate Amount
content:
# Financing Account Standing and the Late-Rate Amount

Window Replacement Contracts. The payment record of the contract's Ridgeline Home Improvement Financing account sets an account-standing share in the late-rate amount of a late balance charge.

**Rule.** The account-standing share comes from the contract's financing account in force: with no late fee and no returned payment posted on it in the last twelve months and at least one payment posted on it, it is the clean-paying share of 0.5; with no late fee and no returned payment in the last twelve months and no payment posted on it yet, it is the clean-new share of 0.8; otherwise, including a contract with no financing account in force, it is one.

The contract's financing account in force is its account that is approved, active, delinquent or paid off; a cancelled or charged-off account is never read, and entries on any other account of the household do not enter the share. The share multiplies the series monthly rate and the late-charge balance in the late-rate amount for one period, before that amount is rounded to the cent.

| Financing account in force on the contract | Late fee or returned payment on it in the last 12 months | Payments ever posted on it | Share |
|---|---|---|---|
| Yes | None | At least one | 0.5 |
| Yes | None | None | 0.8 |
| Yes | One or more | Any | 1 |
| None | — | — | 1 |

## Hypothetical readings

- A contract whose account in force shows regular payments and no late fee or returned payment in the last year, while the household's older, charged-off account carries a late fee: 0.5.
- A late-charge balance of $10,000 at a hypothetical monthly rate of 2% with a share of 0.5 gives a late-rate amount of $100.00 for the period.
